# `server-url-changed`

A servers URL changed or was removed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` |
| **Rule IDs** | `server-url-changed` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Paths and operations ([RULES.md section 2](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A server URL was removed from `servers` at the document, path or operation level. Adding a URL is not reported.

## Why this default

Clients configured with the removed base URL send requests to the wrong place. It is a warning because clients often configure the base URL themselves.

## Example

From test case [`server-url-changed-document`](../../test/cases/server-url-changed-document/): A document-level server URL removed is reported once, not per operation.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
    version: 1.0.0
  servers:
- - url: https://api.example.com/v1
+ - url: https://api.example.com/v2
  paths:
    '/pets':
```

Findings:

- `server-url-changed` · warn · document

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

Options for this rule:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `compare` | `full` | `full`, `path` (ignore host changes, e.g. per environment) or `off`. |

```yaml
rules:
  server-url-changed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep the old server URL working, or announce the move.
